name: SteelSeries Rival 5 Wired Optical Mouse
comments:
I wanted a mouse that didn't have rubber grips or a bunch of unnecessary aesthetic grooves as those get nasty over time. This mouse looks clean, has nice RGB, and feels good in my hand. I bought it more for the look and feel than all the extra buttons, but I have been finding them quite useful now that I've started using them. My favorite thing I've done with one of the buttons is assign one of them the shortcut for enabling/disabling HDR so I don't have to press 3 separate keys every time I want to switch it on/off. Another great feature is the cord; instead of an inflexible rubber cord, this mouse's cord is a very flexible mesh which doesn't get stuck on the edge of my desk or get stuck being bunched up.
Out of all the devices within my setup, my SteelSeries mouse and keyboard have the best accompanying software (SteelSeries GG). Sure, there is a lot of bloated garbage I am never, ever going to use (like 3D aim trainer), but all manufacturer specific programs have some nonsense in them, and SteelSeries GG doesn't turn all of the nonsense features on like some other programs.
The RGB and button-assigning portion of the software (Engine tab) is highly customizable and allows for syncing between different SteelSeries devices. The RGB offers better customization than any of the other RGB software I have to use, and makes me wish that SteelSeries GG was compatible with non-SteelSeries devices. My favorite feature is that it allows you to customize specific colors for effects that use multiple colors. Most of my devices will allow an unchangeable rainbow effect for multi-colored modes, but SteelSeries GG will let me set my own spectrum of colors to shift through. My only option for customizable multi-color on other RGB devices is to manually set different static colors for individual LEDs. Also, unlike some of my other RGB devices, the mouse retains its settings when the computer is restarted or awakes from sleep mode. For example, my AIO uses NZXT CAM for its RGB, and it is completely hit or miss whether the RGB decides to turn on when I start up. My SteelSeries mouse is ready with the last loaded lighting profile as soon as my PC comes on.
Overall very happy with this mouse.

comments:
This might be the best mouse I’ve ever owned. Great color, cool lighting effects, and it’s especially amazing when paired with the docking station.
Years ago, I had the first version of the Razer Mamba, and it came with a dock that looked like a podium. Back then, charging was done through contact pins, so you had to place the mouse correctly — not difficult, but still required a bit of care. It also had the option to work either wirelessly through the dock or with a special-shaped cable that plugged directly into the mouse.
Now, things are so much better. The docking station magnetically snaps the mouse into place, just like Apple’s MagSafe. 😄 The dongle is hidden under the bottom cover of the mouse, so you can take it with you, plug it into any device, and keep using the mouse wirelessly — no need to carry the dock around. There’s also Bluetooth support, and any USB-C cable works fine for charging (unless it’s too bulky to fit).
The only weird thing is the protruding side button. It’s not recognized as a separate button — you can only assign it to mimic a keypress or macro (or anything available in the Razer app). But this makes it impossible to use properly in games.
By “properly” I mean having it recognized as something like Mouse6, instead of being treated as some random key you’ve assigned to it, leaving you wondering why it feels so inconvenient. 😬

I love this mouse. I can change basically everything about it how I'd like it to be. I can change the amount of DPI settings on the mouse, change the speed of the DPI with each setting, and I can custom make color schemes to put on the mouse itself even though I like the default settings best! :]
Been using this for years.
I am no pro gamer, but so far this mouse has proven very reliable and comfortable to use, and for the price I paid for it is a no-brainer.
love the viper mini! i have small hands so the mini fits perfect:)

Out of my entire list, this is the best value. I really can't recommend this mouse enough-its got super smooth skates, a lightweight body, a comfortable shape and ultra satisfying lightweight/low travel clicks. You can't even feel the cable, which is very long as well. It also has some rgb on the logo, and right below your palm. This mouse smashes all my expectations in every category. And it's literally only 30 dollars.
Really good, lightweight mouse. I ended up getting a new one because my hands were a bit too large for it.
Great size for smaller hands. Very light weight if you like that type of mouse.
Low response time mouse which works well and is cheap.

name: Glorious Model I 2 Wireless/Bluetooth/Wired Optical Mouse
comments: love this mouse! looks nice, feels nice. my only slight complaint is that there's no pinky rest, but that doesnt personally bother me all too much

name: Razer DeathAdder V2 Wired Optical Mouse
comments: It’s a great mouse, I’ve had mine for 2 years and it looks and feels fantastic.
Great mouse, been using it for years now and have had no problems at all.
It's a great value mouse, super accurate, very light and comfortable

I absolutely love razer products. I know a lot of people hate on them because of the price. Or say that they go bad. But I have always used razer and their products last me YEARS. I own 6 different razer products all currently in use.
Didnt get it yet, but Sound good
It clicks in the moment when your brain just relaises there is an enemy. Very fast, feels good in your hands and I know I will have it until the last atom wears out.
great mice, so many options, great software, can combine with other hw, games setings, for that price, steal
its a mouse. kinda expensive ig maybe i shouldve gotten a logitech. anyway i like the side buttons and the length feels nice
Nothing to write home about really but it's not super lightweight and feels nice in the hand but there are better alternatives out there.
Honestly, at MSRP this mouse isn't worth it, try to find it used for cheap or on sale if you can.

name: Redragon M908 IMPACT MMO Wired Optical Mouse
comments: Have used this mouse now for almost three years without any issues. The software needs some getting used to it but it is a really nice alternative to the RAZOR Naga which costs a whole lot more.
Got this 37.50 off. It is great!

Single best mouse I have ever used, feels more responsive and comfortable than any expensive mouse I have put my hands on. The num-pad is fantastic for anything, I use it for fps games as it allows you to keep your finders on wasd and use your thumb for your hotkeys. For $30, this STOMPS most competition.

name: Corsair HARPOON RGB PRO Wired Optical Mouse
comments:
I used to use a Red Dragon Mouse and Keyboard Combo that I bought off Amazon and I can honestly say that you can feel the quality differences big time. I decided with the new upgrade of my gaming PC that I would spoil myself with some quality parts to include the mouse and keyboard. I casually game with AAA titles so I look for comfort and simplicity with my computer gaming needs. For my mouse I decided on this one as it matches with my Corsair K70 Keyboard. I personally never used a wireless mouse or keyboard so I just stuck with wired option as I do not mind having a direct connection.
PROS: The first thing I noticed is that this mouse has a total of 5 buttons which fit very comfortably with my right hand. The mouse itself is very light and does not have the beaming red optical light that some mice do. It does also include a RGB for the Corsair icon which is a nice touch. So far I have tested it quick action FPS such as Overwatch, Counter-Strike and Doom Eternal. I can say that this mouse is very sleek, light and comfortable for gaming.
CONS: None so far.
Overall I am very happy with this purchase and highly recommend for anyone looking for a simple gaming mouse for their needs.
A good mouse that works well and is easy-to-use.

I got this mouse for $25 on Black Friday as a part of a keyboard + mouse combo deal. You definitely pay for what you get in terms of build quality at that price but an RGB mouse for only $25 is a steal. Personally I would pay an extra bit of money and get something like a Razer Deathadder V2 but it's really down to personal preference when it comes to peripherals so this does the job for now.
There is no reason to spend more than $25 on a mouse. This shows it. High-quality switches, 6 buttons, and an RGB light that runs with Corsair's ICue software.
The finish on this feels great for pretty much any grip, the programmable buttons on the side are very useful in hotkey-intensive games. DPI switch is flexible and easy to use. Great mouse.
Love the shape, love the feel. I use a fingertip/claw grip and I have large hands.
This mouse is among of the best ive ever used.
It points, it clicks, AND it lights up!
Great mouse, DPI settings were exciting.
its a good budget mouse, also rgb and u can use ique to custom it. dpi can be custom too in ique.

name: Asus ROG HARPE ACE AIM LAB EDITION Wireless/Wired Optical Mouse

specs.Part #:
P713 ROG HARPE ACE AIM LAB EDITION/BLK
90MP02W0-BMAA00
90mp02w0-bmua00

comments: Amazing how light these guys are these days. Side buttons slightly awkward and an RBG logo would have been cool...although the wheel RGB is quality.

I've used this mouse for nearly a year with my laptop and it performs great. Everything saves to the hardware so there's no need to use the terrible Armoury Crate software all this time. Also very flexible in terms of being both wired and wireless.

name: Logitech MX MASTER 3S Wireless Optical Mouse
comments: Very impressed with this mouse for being wireless. The included software really helps with productivity.

This mouse feels incredible. It fits my hand really well and I can use it for a long time without feeling strained. The unlockable scroll wheel is a nice touch too, although as a neurodivergent person, I really only use it as a fidget toy :D The thumb rest is very big and made of some very nice rubbery material. It makes for a great user experience since my hand never touches my mouse pad. Very nice! Three minor pain points:
You can't use this mouse in wired mode because it only charges over USB-C
The thumb rest attracts finger gunk and can become discolored - don't use this mouse with cheeto dust on your fingers!
Mine stopped working randomly - this is kind of a common issue with this mouse because Logitech's QA tends to ignore slightly loose contacts with the internal battery - at least that's what Reddit told me. Send it back to Logitech to get it fixed for free.
Super precise and with a soft surface
I love the feel and responsiveness of this mouse, but I have yet to use it for its' intended purpose. Its' software isn't great though, possibly user error.

name: Logitech G502 X Wired Optical Mouse
comments: Great quality build but i consider it to be overpriced and i hate the wire. it looks good tho and feels good to i like the extra side clicks. if youd like something better for the price and wireless i would recommand the Razer Basilisk V3 X HyperSpeed there is nothing wrong with the mouse.

I got this because it was one of the only wired white mice out there that were similar to the Razer basilisk mice that I usually use, much lighter than the Razer basilisk though. I only wish the cable was braided like the Razer mice, 4.7/5 stars.

name: Razer Basilisk V3 Pro 35K Optical Mouse
Logitech G705 Wireless/Wired/Bluetooth Optical Mouse
comments: favorite mouse for small hands, rgb is pretty and has a really great battery life so i don’t charge it for a couple days after all nighters of gaming.

name: Corsair NIGHTSABRE RGB Wireless/Bluetooth/Wired Optical Mouse
Corsair SCIMITAR ELITE WIRELESS MMO Wireless/Bluetooth/Wired Optical Mouse
Corsair M75 Wireless/Bluetooth/Wired Optical Mouse
Logitech G402 Wired Optical Mouse
comments: Have been using this since 2016, will be replacing with a Basilisk V3 Pro or a G502, still works like new with very little wear and tear. Only downside was the software, it's honestly terrible but recently seems to have improved, no longer crashes and finally recognizes games automatically now.
I have large hands and this fits my hand shape nearly perfectly. The extra buttons are a bit gimmicky but Logitech software makes it easy to disable them or reconfigure.

Great wired mouse for not too much money. Loads of buttons for me - the back and forward especially makes web browsing easy. the left and right click plus the wheel which has a click function. Also it has 3 buttons to adjust the DPI - two work as up and down DPI selection and the last button sets to 400DPI which is good for FPS games when you need to accurately aim at the target.
Perfect mouse for palm grip and if you have large hands.
I love this mouse, got it for discount at Christmas and it is honestly amazing, I only wish you could change the LED color but no stars off because of the great performance

I got it for £18 during Black Friday 2020. It has got "only" 4000 DPI, but what many people do not realise is the fact that IRL you do not use more than 500-2000 (unless you're doing anything other than gaming).
It tracks superbly, I have been using it at mainly 1000-2000DPI and has not missed a "dot per inch".
Got all the DPI settings in the palm and is light-weight (vs G502). Can't ask for much after going with the Hyperion Fury.

Now, this is a proper gaming mouse. Not the best one in the market but right up there with them. Doesn't have a ton of features, but more than you'll need. The only upgrade over this will be a massive overkill G502. Anyway, back to my piece. The Logitech logo with the LED can only be set to a hue of blue and can be given a breathing effect. There's a DPI indicator LED as well. Comes with 8 programmable buttons, which is more than I ever need. Lightweight, smooth movement. This mouse is massive, might not fit into your hand if you have small ones. All in all, money well spent. Absolutely loving it.
Got this on sell for 31$ it was nearly half price of g502 hero and I'm really happy about it, great mouse.

The reason why I specifically bought this was the DPI buttons being on the side of the mouse instead of the top. I always hit them when on the top. This mouse has a great grip. It fits right in your palm. I've been using this for a while and it is showing no signs of wear.

name: Razer Viper Ultimate Wireless Optical Mouse
comments: Holds a good charge , easily reprogramable

Super lightweight and great hand feel for my claw grip. The included charging dock is super cool and makes life so much easier as well. My only minor complaint is that the side buttons are a bit more recessed than I would like, but it's understandable for an ambidextrous mouse. It's also not a deal breaker by any means, as those side buttons are still comfortable to press while gaming, just not quite as comfortable as something like a Logitech G502.

name: Glorious MODEL O Wired Optical Mouse
comments: Had some issues with the cable connection in the past but I replaced the cable. Sometimes I have issues with the mouse but it is light and movement is great. I have a Razer Viper V2 Pro I may replace this with.
I've seen a lot of YouTubers recommending this mouse, and I really like it. Right-clicking feels a bit weird, like it's a bit sticky, but I think that might just be a one-off mistake.

Flawless mouse. I have no complaints whatsoever, the software is amazing, it feels amazing on my hand, and you are able to perform things like drag clicks, along with being allowed to edit the debounce time is phenomenal.
Light and quite nice to look at.
Lightweight

7/10) Mouse snobs will go on about the "horrible build quality" of this mouse, but I haven't had any of those issues. Does it's job well, It's light and feels great in my hand. The only points off are for weird-ish looks and a meh cable.

Don't listen to the hype, unless the regular model o or the model o wireless are better, I just cannot recommend this brand. Within 4 DAYS of having this mouse, the left mouse button started to have a lot of pretravel. I went onto a forum and they(glorious) said that the pretravel was within their QC. Their QC must be god awful. I am never buying another product from glorious again, absolute dogcrap. Not to mention the unholy amount of case creaking that emanates from this piece of trash is you so much as TAP the top of the case. Do not recommend. The hype was fake in my opinion. Switching to corsair.
Light, quick, great softweare, and one of the best mouses I have ever owned.
Super light, gorgeous, hella light cable, great software. AMAZING MOUSE!
Great mouse. Love this mouse a lot. Not much else to say.

name: HP HyperX Pulsefire Haste Wireless Optical Mouse
comments: Light, good looking, and great response time for a budget wireless mouse.
I would recommend this mouse every single day of the week.

name: Asus ROG Chakram X Origin Wired/Wireless/Bluetooth Optical Mouse
Glorious MODEL D Wired Optical Mouse
comments:
Good mouse, I like the lighting on it, has a really good sensor for the price, and it's software isn't horrendously bad.
After about 2 years of use, both the left and right mouse button have become VERY light to click. Just resting my fingers on them will cause them to click.
I'll likely be buying a new mouse here soon, but it is a nice mouse for about $50.

I can't even describe how many I tried. Razer, Rapoo, Logitech, HyperX etc. Had at least a dozen. This one exceeds everything. It's perfect in every aspect. Sure, the RGB isn't the easiest to configure, but I seriously can't explain how good this mouse is. It's perfect.
light mouse :)

Great mouse for the price. Good build quality, great skates, great tracking, great switches, great feel, great scroll wheel (some people might not like it), super light cord, practically weightless, big for larger hands, decent software, and amazing price.
Comfy, and glides well. Also has great RGB.

(NEW, GIFT) This mouse has the least problematic software of all the mice I use with this build, and that is because of how meek and basic the software is. Besides the software, this mouse feels amazing in first-person games and action-oriented games, as it is slim, breathable, responsive, and glides like an angel. It is a rather minimal mouse for the price, however this is usually what type of mouse most people are interested in, and in that category, it is one of the highest of it's class.
Practically weightless. This is so much lighter than my corsair iron claw and I love it.
Really good mice. The only potentially bad thing is that the honeycomb shape on the top might accumulate some skin residue if that's a problem for you.

Not to mention the hilarious branding, but the Glorious Model D feels so good in the hand, so lightweight, and with quality pads it comes with, it simply glides along your mousepad, and feels like air - it feels so good, and is more ergonomic than my old Razer Deathadder Chroma. Not to mention the customizable RGB with the side lights - this mouse has style. The complimentary stickers were also a nice bonus. Glorious - we NEED a MMORPG/MOBA version of the Model D! That would be heaven.

Looks fantastic, build quality is solid and light. The software that is used to change DPI, macros, lighting effects etc is very easy to use and works great. The buttons are fairly light compared to the old Dell mice I'm used to and it slides beautifully. Once I've been using it for a while and gotten better used to it I will probably update this review and change it to 5 stars (as it feels amazing so far).

name: Logitech MX Master 3 Wireless Laser Mouse
comments: Been using this as my daily driver for years - would be really hard to go back to any other model at this point. I do the feel the rubber isn't the best element to weather years of abuse and doesn't age as well as metal, but it's a small price to pay for the ergonomics. I had a terrible experience with its Bluetooth connection, borderline unusable because of the lag/choppiness. Fortunately the Bolt receiver is far more reliable and I have not experienced any trouble with it.
Used the first gen model for many years and was more than satisfied with it. So far the current gen Master continues that trend
Great productivity mouse, feels just right in the hand and love it for my work use cases.

Amazing Bluetooth + wireless receiver mouse for creative work. Mappable buttons per program with magnetic scroll wheel that operates in 2 modes. Free scroll and line-by-line precision scrolling. Easily switch across 3 devices linked via Bluetooth pair or wherever the wireless receiver is plugged in. USB C charging for quick recharge and lasts for days

Probably not for gamers, and maybe not for people with smaller hands, but I love this thing. The weighted magnetic scroll wheel makes scrolling a breeze, the side scroller makes spreadsheets just a little more fun, and the back and forward thumb buttons are great for browsing (and probably other things, but I haven't gotten used to all the other uses yet).
One downside is that while the device is compatible with Linux, the software that comes with it is not. This means Linux button customization is difficult/limited. Still 5 stars though.
Lost connection via wireless a few times and the logitech software lost its settings a few times too but otherwise excellent.
best productivity mouse imo. love it so much, i bought another, one at home, one in office. works seamlessly between mac & windows

Hands down the best mouse you can get for MacOS functionality (or in general). Extremely ergonomic, beefy battery life, full charges in under 15-20 min via USB-C, endless customization options per Application (requires Logitech Options or Options Plus, both free software).

For creativity/productivity/office use, this is a good mouse. Plenty of customizability and functionality for any user. It is fairly comfortable, but the Razer Pro Click is a step ahead of the MX Master 3 for comfort due to a better shape and far lower weight. All connectivity options are equally viable but I believe the 2.4GHz receiver to be the superior method. Battery life is excellent and I almost never need to worry about getting too low. If I had to choose between the MX Master 3 or the Razer Pro Click, I would rather use the Razer Pro Click.
very high weight (~141g)
long battery life
good connectivity options (with USB-C connector!)
infinite scroll wheel
no exact DPI adjustment ("Pointer Speed" slider is all you get)
very low polling rate (125 Hz)
fairly loud clicks with questionable switch reliability
Both fully supported on Linux using Solaar and using a single Logitech Unifying receiver (single USB-A Port taken).

name: Corsair HARPOON RGB Wireless Optical Mouse
comments: Ehhh it's a good mouse I've had it for a couple of years now.

A little pricey for what it is, but then again, you do get the advantage of wirelessness. Good if you want a mouse that's simple but still quality. Maybe a nitpick, but the RGB can seem a little flickery sometimes in how it transitions between colors; it's not as smooth as my Corsair keyboard. Doesn't matter a lot of the time, though, since your hand will cover it.
It feels great in my hand and has a nice tight response. I got mine on sale though.

I’ve had this mouse for almost two years, this is the mouse I’ve had before I built this PC. Still works great and the battery on it is fantastic.
If you like simple mice like I do, the Corsair harpoon RGB is a great choice.

I've used this mouse for a but now and it's a great value mouse. It's wireless and has RGB - that's all I wanted. The battery life is plenty for me and the sensor is good enough. It doesn't fit my hand perfectly but it was a good value so I got it.

Very satisfied. Can be used wired (special micro-USB cable) or wireless (with special dongle or Bluetooth). You can put the dongle inside the mouse if you need to move with it for some reason. Even though I personally only use it wired, I would advise you to take this one instead of the other versions. Having the choice between wired and wireless is very convenient and totally worth the price difference (even though I paid mine less than the normal version somehow). I have also noticed that, unlike this one, the wire on the wired version isn't centered. Pretty sure it must be annoying. You can create different profiles (with iCUE) and switch on the fly between them. More buttons than I personally need, but might not be enough for some people. I find it very comfortable (I'd say I have neither small nor big hands), but I can understand some people don't (mostly depending on their hand position). The best, as usual, would be to try it before buying. Pretty sure it's not good for lefties though.

It's a mouse, and it does mouse stuff well. It's Corsair's basic RGB gaming mouse, with the Corsair logo lighting up, and a DPI switch with a back/forward button on the left side of the mouse. It's all I need in a mouse, I do wish the battery lasted a bit longer but I knew it wouldn't be as good as my non-gaming wireless mouse in the battery department - a given.
After a few years it seems to have gotten a bit choppy movement-wise. I've got a Razer Basilisk V3 Pro now with this bad larry as a backup. Still, it is a solid entry level gaming mouse.
Great mouse, however the wireless USB adaptor stopped working for me unfortunately so I am using it as a wired mouse

Got it for $20 a while back and I'm very impressed that it is still in basically perfect condition although a little dirty. It's fast, looks good, cheap, good battery life, and will make me never use wired mice again.
Bit of a latency issue when plugged in, only fix is to either reconnect it or unplug and use wireless mode. Otherwise a good mouse for everyday use, even wirelessly.

name: Glorious Model O 2 Wired/Wireless/Bluetooth Optical Mouse
Logitech G604 LIGHTSPEED Wireless Optical Mouse
comments:
Logitech and discontinuing great products, name a more iconic duo. I wish I bought like 10 of these back when they were 60 bucks each. I'm gonna be real sad when I can't use this mouse anymore. 6 tactile side buttons in a rectangle, on-board memory, unlockable scroll wheel, big and heavy. Literally a perfect mouse. The only thing out there that's similar is the Naga Pro 2 but that thing's $150 minimum.
Bit of advice to anyone with a wireless Logitech mouse: If you can get away with it, get Ghub off your computer. I don't know why but this mouse's battery life literally tripled or more when I saved my mouse buttons in Ghub to the on-board memory and uninstalled Ghub.

Great wireless mouse, with Logitech's amazing lightspeed wireless connection. I adore all the buttons on the mouse, actually helps a lot both in productivity and gaming. The only thing I DESPISE about this mouse is Logitech's terrible G-Hub software, its atrocious and hard to use.

Over 1000 hours of gaming use, I love this mouse and love its design, completely reprogrammable. Any other mouse feels weird to use because I'm so used to it, it's nice that it uses an AA battery because it lasts so long I've only changed it 3 times, the dpi settings on the mouse are also nice for precision. I wish this mouse would never wear out or break. I've had this mouse for a little over 3 years now btw, I'm gonna be heart broken when it dies of old age and lots of use.

A bang for the buck mouse for MMO, simulator, and complicated games.
The downside is the poor durability of the switches.
I have used the G503 for a lot of years on my old computer so I got the newer version for the new computer. Works the same and has the 6 thumb buttons.

Meh. All I want is a simple mouse that offers a click button for hyper scroll. I don't need all the extra side buttons and fancy junk. So this was the compromise to use the reliable "Lightspeed" connection and have hyper scroll.
Overall though, I think Logitech has lost a lot of their footing and every single newer product I have purchased from them has been total junk. It's been 0 for 4 products so I gave up. Actually kind of shocked this mouse is still working, but the flap on the thumb side is loose.
The Logitech software is very annoying but once you have it set up with works great.

Best mouse for MOBA. Decent quality. The plastic quality is not as good as G602 (old model) but wcyd. Theres an issue with the on board chip of this mouse. If you plan to use this mouse with no software it might bug out on you and click twice for every click you do. I'm not sure whats causes this to happen but if you run the software everything works perfectly. It has bluetooth and 2.5GH USB reciever so you can switch between 2 computers if you hold the wifi button for 1 sec.

I love the overall feel of the mouse itself, and I like that it's wireless. However, I'm on my 2nd G604 mouse. Luckily, Logitech warranty is great. The side buttons make me continue to use this and non of the others.

Since my g903 burnt down inside literally I wanted something fresh, I was already failiar with the G502 shape and the hero sensor from 903 but I wanted somthing different. I came up on this and It feels like a more refinded version of the g502. I had one issue wherethe right click was rubbing on something which got alleviated within a couple weeks

name: MSI CLUTCH Wired Optical Mouse
Logitech G102 LIGHTSYNC RGB Wired Optical Mouse
HP HyperX Pulsefire Haste 2 Bluetooth/Wireless/Wired Optical Mouse
comments: I was worried that i would hate how it felt in the hand as I was coming from a logitech m325 and my other attempts at getting a better mouse like the mx master 3 cause hand pain, but it feels great for my grip.
Drag clicking without tape has a learning curve, but everything else is great.

name: SteelSeries Rival 650 Wireless Wireless Optical Mouse
comments:
Had a SteelSeries Rival 500 before which I loved but wanted to go for something wireless. This seemed like a logical choice and has so far been every bit as good as I'd hoped. I cannot tell any difference whatsoever in terms of lag when it's plugged in compared to when it's not, which is all I can say really!
For the price (still available the right side of £50) you can't go wrong.

its not the lightest out there, but i like it, i like heavy mice. Only complaint would be the side rubber pieces, they seem to fall off after maybe a year of use. To fix it you can glue them back on like i did.

Beautiful mouse, clean RGB design, great controlling software and battery lasts days (for my usage). Fits my hand really well and the adjustable weights is a nice touch. Controlling software and DPI/Profile settings are great for all types of games.
Steelseries, switched to them after using Razer for years but noticed that quality decreased. Very happy with the change.
Great wireless mouse at an acceptable price.
No delay, perfect weight

This is a good option for people who enjoy having a wireless mouse, and also being able to adjust the weights on it as well. It enjoys having the ability to be personalized in many ways through SteelSeries Engine 3, but keep in mind the RGB if you're always running wireless.
